The persisted-state guard has the same gap: a risk_score of NaN becomes 100.0 (maximum risk) instead of the default 0.0, so a malformed kernel file looks maximally risky after restart until the next assess() overwrites the field.

The new malformed-input tests only use strings, so the non-finite path (NaN/+inf) is not covered even though it is the case that bypasses the guards. Add regression coverage for record_evaluation, record_drift and a persisted NaN risk_score.

findings.message: A non-finite rate (NaN or +inf) passes float() and Python's min/max turn it into 1.0, so a NaN drift score becomes maximum drift instead of keeping the previous value. That contradicts the docstring and ADR-062's promise that malformed rate inputs keep the previous value, and can silently raise or hide governance risk.

The persisted-state guard has the same gap: a risk_score of NaN becomes 100.0 (maximum risk) instead of the default 0.0, so a malformed kernel file looks maximally risky after restart until the next assess() overwrites the field.

The new malformed-input tests only use strings, so the non-finite path (NaN/+inf) is not covered even though it is the case that bypasses the guards. Add regression coverage for record_evaluation, record_drift and a persisted NaN risk_score.

The persisted-state guard has the same gap: a risk_score of NaN becomes 100.0 (maximum risk) instead of the default 0.0, so a malformed kernel file looks maximally risky after restart until the next assess() overwrites the field.
